summary:
At 8:00 PM on 4 August 2026, the Low-Pressure Area (LPA) located west of Bacnotan, La Union intensified into Tropical Depression MAYMAY, according to the Philippine Atmospheric, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (PAGASA).

By 2:00 AM on 5 August 2026, Tropical Depression MAYMAY further intensified into Tropical Storm MAYMAY (international name: Kujira) while moving slowly near the western coast of Northern Luzon.

On 6 August 2026, Tropical Storm MAYMAY weakened into a Tropical Depression and made landfall over the Ilocos Sur–La Union area before traversing the mountainous terrain of Northern Luzon. As it moved inland, the system continued to weaken while crossing the rugged terrain and is forecast to emerge over the eastern coastal waters of Isabela or Cagayan. PAGASA indicated that the cyclone may further weaken into a remnant low by the afternoon or evening, although interaction with the mountainous terrain could result in an earlier weakening. The remnant low is then expected to move generally southeastward before merging with the larger circulation of Tropical Cyclone DOLPHIN.

Despite its weakening, MAYMAY, together with the enhanced Southwest Monsoon, continues to bring heavy rainfall, strong to gale-force winds, and hazardous sea conditions over affected areas. PAGASA also emphasized that localities outside the forecast track and confidence cone may still experience significant impacts, particularly heavy rainfall, strong winds, and rough to very rough seas.
name: Philippines: Southwest Monsoon enhanced by Tropical Cyclones Maymay and Dolphin, 2026
